summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Avalon GPU Systems. Discussed integration patterns (resell / marketplace / OEM), joint benchmarking on H100/A100, compliance (SOC2/SSO/KMS), and next steps for a technical deep dive and sample workload exchange.
transcript:
Date: 2026-12-28
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lucas Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood Partnerships), Rajiv Patel (Avalon Head of Partnerships), Elena Kovacs (Avalon Solutions Architect), Tommy Lin (Avalon Biz Dev), Diego Marquez (Avalon Infra)

Summary: quick intros, partnership models, technical constraints, benchmarking plan, compliance questions, next steps and action items.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, um Maya from Redwood here, i'm the partner lead on this region, appreciate you taking the time
[00:07] Rajiv Patel: thanks Maya, Rajiv here, excited to chat, quick intros on our side: elena, tommy, diego are here, we run hardware and partner sales for Avalon
[00:15] Lucas Rivera: hi all Lucas from Redwood infra, i'll be the technical owner for any benching and private deployment convo
[00:22] Elena Kovacs: yeah hi, we mostly do OEM GPU racks and cloud appliances, curious how Redwood sees partner integrations, also curious about dedicated and private options
[00:33] Maya Chen: great, quick agenda - mutual intros, go over partner motions (resell, marketplace, joint bench), tech constraints (vpc/onprem, sso, kms), then next steps
[00:42] Tommy Lin: perfect
[00:45] [00:45] Rajiv Patel: one quick thing - we're fielding inquiries from mid-market enterprises that want a managed inference offering with regional data residency; wondering if Redwood can fit that offering model
[00:58] Maya Chen: absolutely we have three deployment modes: hosted api for fast time-to-value, dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and private (vpc/on-prem) for regulated workloads - all expose same api surface so partner integration can be pretty seamless
[01:12] Diego Marquez: when you say private on prem, is that basically customer-managed control plane or do you still manage any services?
[01:20] Lucas Rivera: good q — private means customer-managed networking and optional on-prem package; Redwood provides a control plane that can run in a customer's VPC or in a closed environment depending on agreement, and we have KMS integrations for key management — HSM is supported via standard integrations.
[01:37] Elena Kovacs: what about SOC2 logs and audit, that's table stakes for our customers
[01:42] Maya Chen: yep SOC2, audit logs, RBAC, SAML SSO - we can scope full compliance packet; will share security docs after the call
[01:50] [02:02] Tommy Lin: on the commercial side, do you support marketplace listings or resell? we do both and want to understand options
[02:09] Maya Chen: we support multiple partner motions: referral, resell, marketplace integrations; can do co-sell where Avalon provides infra and Redwood provides the inference layer and ops — or a white-labeled private deployment for large customers
[02:25] Rajiv Patel: pricing model? is it usage-based only or do you do reserved commitments for partners?
[02:32] Maya Chen: hosted api is usage-based; for Dedicated we do reserved capacity contracts (monthly/annual commits). For partner resell we can map an OEM/reseller pricing layer over reserved capacity — we should look at expected throughput and concurrency to size it properly
[02:46] [03:10] Lucas Rivera: from the technical side, to run good benchmarks we usually ask for representative workloads — average prompt length, peak concurrent requests, response size, and preferred model families (LLaMA-3, Mixtral, etc). Also need HW spec (A100, H100, memory configs, NVLink) to pick quantization and kernel profiles
[03:30] Elena Kovacs: we have H100 blades and upcoming custom boards; we can share spec sheet. we typically see request patterns of short prompts with high qps for our low-latency customers
[03:45] Lucas Rivera: perfect, that maps to what we call latency-sensitive workloads; Redwood has options: continuous batching, prefix/KV cache, and quantization profiles to hit both latency SLOs and lower unit cost
[03:58] Rajiv Patel: any constraints on models you onboard? our customers want choices — some ask for GPT-style, others LLaMA derivatives
[04:07] Maya Chen: we maintain a model catalog with curated open models and verified performance profiles — and we can onboard customer models but there is an onboarding window to validate perf and safety. also we support function calling, streaming, and structured outputs so integration patterns are flexible
[04:25] [04:40] Tommy Lin: curious about latency numbers — do you have ballpark p99s for H100 with typical transformer models?
[04:47] Lucas Rivera: p99 depends a lot on prompt length and seq length; for a 1-2k token context on an H100 single-shot generate you can expect sub-200ms p99 for some optimized models with our kernels and KV cache, but i'll caveat that this varies; that's why we do partner benching
[05:05] Diego Marquez: ok good, benching seems critical, what does a bench engagement look like?
[05:12] Lucas Rivera: we usually do: exchange workload/spec, agree on metric targets (latency, tpm, cost per token), run an H100 and A100 run, compare quantization profiles (8-bit/4-bit) and batching configs, then produce a bench report with perf profiles and a recommended config for Dedicated or Private deployment
[05:30] Rajiv Patel: do you run the bench in our infra or in Redwood test infra?
[05:36] Maya Chen: either — for initial validation we can run in Redwood infra or our lab. for final proof we prefer running on customer infra or partner infra to capture real network and topology effects — sounds like Avalon would prefer that
[05:50] Elena Kovacs: yes we'd like the bench to run on our blades, since NVLink and host topology matter a lot
[05:57] Lucas Rivera: makes sense, we'll need access to run controlled workloads — we can provide containerized runners and test harness; minimal firewall/NAT config is usually required
[06:10] [06:25] Tommy Lin: any integrations with partner marketplaces? we list solutions in our partner portal and want Redwood to be discoverable
[06:32] Maya Chen: we do marketplace listings and joint marketing; partnerships team (cc'd Priya) will follow up to map GTM activities and co-marketing slots
[06:42] Priya Kapoor: hey all, i'll pick up GTM and partner ops follow-ups — happy to work on a joint plan
[06:48] Rajiv Patel: security - KMS and key ownership is a big ask, can customers retain keys?
[06:55] Lucas Rivera: yes customer-managed KMS is supported, keys can be retained by customer; you can plug in your KMS/HSM via our integrations, we do not hold plaintext keys in hosted flows by default
[07:10] Elena Kovacs: data residency and logs - do you provide audit logs at token level or request level?
[07:16] Maya Chen: per-request and token-level cost breakdowns are available in Redwood Console, and audit logs can be exported to SIEM or S3 depending on privacy needs
[07:30] [07:50] Rajiv Patel: what about SLA and support for Dedicated customers? we need an enterprise SLA for some deals
[07:57] Maya Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets, configurable autoscaling and burst options. support tiers available — we can scope an enterprise package for Avalon customers
[08:10] Diego Marquez: network egress costs — if the model is hosted in Avalon region how do you handle egress and cost split for joint customers?
[08:20] Maya Chen: that depends on the partner model — if Avalon is providing infra then egress costs sit with Avalon; for hosted we have a standard egress model; in resell situations we can do pass-through cost or bundle into a deal line item
[08:35] [08:55] Tommy Lin: on legal, any NDAs or standard partner terms we should expect?
[09:01] Maya Chen: we'll share a partner MOU and standard reseller agreement templates — legal intro after we align on commercial motion
[09:10] Rajiv Patel: good. what's the timeline if we wanted to go pilot in Q1?
[09:16] Maya Chen: timeline looks plausible — initial bench and workload exchange in January, tech deep dive mid-January, pilot kickoff late January/early February depending on resource alignment
[09:24] Elena Kovacs: one more technical question — how do you handle model quantization and correctness regression risk? some customers are sensitive to output quality when using 4-bit quantization
[09:35] Lucas Rivera: we run quality monitors and evals tied to prompt sets; Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles by workload and we can run regressions on curated eval sets to ensure quality thresholds aren't broken — fallback to higher precision is possible if quality drops
[09:54] Maya Chen: that's a key differentiator we lean on — quality monitoring and rollback policies during rollouts
[10:05] [10:20] Rajiv Patel: for the pilot we want to measure latency, cost per token, p95/p99, and a small quality eval on our prompts — are those standard?
[10:27] Lucas Rivera: yes we'll include those metrics in the bench report and recommend config for Dedicated vs Private depending on results
[10:35] Diego Marquez: any infra pre-reqs we should prepare for? like firewall rules, container runtime, kernel versions?
[10:42] Lucas Rivera: we'll provide a runbook — usual pre-reqs are container runtime (docker/OCI), minimal port openings for test harness, and optional telemetry hook for perf data, plus root or admin privileges for controlled runs
[11:00] [11:12] Tommy Lin: ok sounds good, what's the ask from Avalon this week?
[11:18] Rajiv Patel: we'll send the hardware spec and two sample workloads, plus a contact for infra access
[11:25] Maya Chen: perfect, we'll send partner deck and bench checklist, and loop Priya on GTM. Lucas will draft the bench harness and share runbook
[11:36] Elena Kovacs: also pls include expected data handling practices for PII — some customers are worried about token retention
[11:44] Maya Chen: yes we'll include data retention policy, opt-in/out for retention, and how logs are handled in private vs hosted setups
[11:52] [12:10] Rajiv Patel: curious - any known gotchas with NVLink topologies? we had a customer with degraded perf because of misconfigured numa/affinity
[12:20] Lucas Rivera: NVLink and PCIe topology definitely matter; we'll run topology-aware configs and check NUMA affinity, and include infra best practices in the runbook
[12:35] Maya Chen: ok let's quickly recap action items and next steps
[12:42] Maya Chen: recap - Redwood: share partner deck (Maya), bench checklist and runbook (Lucas), security packet (Maya). Avalon: share hardware spec and workloads (Elena), identify infra contact (Rajiv). Priya will follow up on GTM. target dates as discussed
[12:58] [13:12] Tommy Lin: sounds good thanks everyone
[13:18] Rajiv Patel: thanks all, excited to move forward
[13:25] Maya Chen: thanks team, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the tech deep dive and share docs
[13:32] Meeting end.

Notes: transcript includes small transcription artifacts and occasional repeated words. References: Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private, Redwood Console, Redwood Optimize, KV cache, quantization, H100/A100, KMS/HSM, SAML/SSO, SOC2.
